label: PF Backlog 663
title: EPIC: Scalability & Capacity Tiers (T1-T4) - capacity model, load evidence, and scale triggers
body: Tracks T1-T4 capacity validation and gated scale-out/in. Source of truth: docs/SCALABILITY-SSOT.md.

brief.problem: PF has no validated enterprise capacity tiers or measured T1/T2 load envelope.
brief.what_adds: Capacity SSOT, T1-T4 targets, load evidence, and scale-out/in triggers.
brief.why: Prevents premature scale-out and unmeasured scale claims.

design_areas.reason: The item exists to validate or gate a PF capacity tier.
Uses existing EDP data plane; no schema change in this tracking item.
No new security surface; measurements must use read-only roles.

BLOCKER: AC-2 unmet: no staging T1/T2 load evidence, restore-drill evidence, benchmark artifacts, capacity report, or HIL acceptance is added; the diff only defines a future plan.
MAJOR: Declared control `CTL-CAPACITY` / `test_edp_slo_config.py` is not touched or evidenced; no fail-able check enforces `CAPACITY_EVIDENCE_MISSING` or `SCALE_TRIGGER_NOT_MET`, so the SSOT remains advisory.
Scale triggers are ambiguous: “DB p95 > 50 ms” has no read/write split and sits at/below the T1 write target (100 ms); DB p99 target is undefined.
SLO table is non-monotonic without rationale: T3 is looser than T2 on API p95/p99, DB read/write, and error rate, which can normalize regressions at enterprise tier.
Security contract missing: no explicit “no tenant data in capacity reports” or read-only benchmark-role requirement in the evidence plan, though the design requires both.
MINOR: Section 6 labels all triggers “measured” but includes contractual SLA/residency triggers; separate measured vs contractual gating.
T4 row is entirely “per cell” with no cell-level SLO targets, making T4 acceptance largely non-falsifiable beyond prose.
Binding SSOT lacks owner/version/date and a HIL approval record despite change control requiring HIL approval.
Capacity report location, redaction rules, and retention are unspecified.
NIT: Docs index description says “T1-T4” while the SSOT also defines T0; align wording.
“T3/T4 are where EDP-24 starts” should explicitly link to trigger conditions and BI-PF-1317/EDP-24 gate.
SUMMARY: The SSOT is directionally strong and preserves trigger-gated T3/T4 plus PF-SB/PF-GP separation, but it is a plan, not validation.
Blocker: AC-2 requires measured T1/T2 load and restore evidence; none is present.
Top risks: advisory-only gates, ambiguous DB triggers, and missing capacity-report redaction/read-only-role guardrails.
